subject: Post-demo: Lumenix SLO alignment & lightweight MAP
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@lumenix.com>, Josh Patel <josh.patel@lumenix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Lumenix SLO alignment & lightweight MAP

Thanks for the time today — good discussion and useful signals on the streaming use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock down an actionable pilot: 

High-level alignment (what we heard)
- Primary workload: streaming responses for agent UI and long-form summarization (avg response length ~220 tokens).
- Traffic shape: spiky during business hours; expect sustained concurrency around 60–80 users with bursts to ~240 users during syncs.
- Golden prompts: 8 canonical prompts across search/summarize/agent flows.

Redwood suggested SLO targets (initial proposal)
- Latency: streaming P95 end-to-end <= 300ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens), P95 <= 650ms for long responses (<= 512 tokens).
- Concurrency: sustain 240 concurrent streaming sessions with <= 1% error rate.
- Throughput: token throughput target aligned to peak bursts (est. 1.2M tokens/hour peak).
- Availability: 99.9% platform + fallback model policy for overload events.

Attachments (attached): lumenix-slo-checklist.csv (baseline targets + measurement plan), demo-recording-20280729.mp4, pilot-mop.docx

Proposed lightweight MAP (mutual action plan)
1) Confirm SLOs and sample traffic: Lumenix provides 48-hour sample traffic file + 8 golden prompts (action: Anna) — due 2028-08-02.
2) Pilot window: Redwood runs a 72-hour dedicated-capacity pilot (isolated pool) to validate P95/P99 and KV cache effectiveness (action: Ben + Marissa) — target start 2028-08-09.
3) Observability: Redwood will share a read-only dashboard and metric contract (token counts, p95/p99 latency, error rate, cache hit ratio). Marissa to own runbook and metric collection.
4) Failover policy: Redwood to provide an auto-fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant when queue depth exceeds threshold; test during pilot.
5) Decision criteria: pass if streaming P95 for short responses <= 350ms and error rate < 2% during pilot and throughput scales to 80%+ of estimated peak.

Open asks from Redwood to Lumenix
- Sample traffic export (48h) + common headers and authentication patterns.
- IP allowlist for test runner and a contact for onboarding SAML (if required).
- Any compliance constraints for trace retention/capture.

If that looks right, please confirm on the dates above or propose alternatives. I’ll get Marissa and our infra team queued for the pilot setup.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Anna Kim <anna.kim@lumenix.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Josh Patel <josh.patel@lumenix.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Lumenix SLO alignment & lightweight MAP

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications before we commit to the 72-hour pilot window: 

1) Latency buckets: Your note differentiates short vs long responses. Can you confirm the exact token boundaries you used (you listed <=128 and <=512, want to validate)? For our UX team, P95 <= 300ms is tight — is that measured from client-side (render-ready) or from request-at-load-balancer?

2) Concurrency vs sessions: Our concurrency estimate is sessions (websocket streams). We’ll validate session counts, but the 240 burst number is realistic. Will Redwood only count active stream connections or in-flight token generation?

3) Cost/estimate: Can you provide a rough pilot cost estimate (ballpark) and whether the fallback model adds incremental cost during overload?

4) Observability: Are the dashboards sampled or full? We need to ensure we can capture request IDs for cross-correlation with our Sentry traces (PII policy applies).

We can provide the traffic export and golden prompts by 2028-08-02. Can you confirm whether Redwood needs any additional headers (we currently strip most telemetry at the LB level)?

—Anna
Anna Kim
Senior Platform Engineer | Lumenix Labs
anna.kim@lumenix.com | +1 206-555-0189

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kim <anna.kim@lumenix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Josh Patel <josh.patel@lumenix.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Lumenix SLO alignment & lightweight MAP

Anna — great questions, answers below and a slightly adjusted acceptance band to keep the pilot pragmatic: 

1) Token boundaries and latency measurement
- Short responses: <= 128 tokens (client render target measured at Redwood edge after final chunk emitted).
- Long responses: <= 512 tokens.
- Measurement point: Redwood measures server-side end-to-end (request in -> last token emitted at edge). We will also surface client-side delta if you can instrument and share request IDs.

2) Concurrency definition
- We count active in-flight generation contexts (open websocket + ongoing token generation). Idle open sockets that are not generating tokens are not counted toward concurrency. We'll provide a clear metric name (in the dashboard) for cross-check.

3) Pilot cost ballpark
- 72-hour dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool: ~USD 4,200 (estimate) — includes three days of reserved GPUs + monitoring and support. Fallback to the cheaper variant only triggers on overload; incremental cost is marginal because payloads are the same but model compute differs (we'll show exact billing in the pilot dashboard).

4) Observability and traces
- Dashboard: full request-level metrics in the pilot (no sampling) with redacted payloads by default. We can add a per-request ID column for cross-correlation; we'll need a sample header your side uses for request IDs (x-lumenix-request-id or similar).

Adjusted decision criteria (pilot pass)
- Short-response streaming P95 <= 350ms (server-edge).
- Long-response streaming P95 <= 700ms.
- Error rate < 2% overall; no single 1-hour window > 4% errors.
- Sustained concurrency handling to 80% of your expected peak (we will simulate spike to full peak but pass criteria require 80% sustained).

Operational asks (what Marissa will need from Lumenix)
- IP allowlist and test CIDR for pilot runner.
- 48-hour traffic export + golden prompts.
- SAML admin contact (only if you want to test private onboarding).

If those adjustments work, I propose we lock pilot start on 2028-08-09. Marissa — can you confirm you can spin up the dashboard and the reserved pool that week?

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments referenced: lumenix-slo-checklist.csv, pilot-mop.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Looping in operational plan and checkpoints we’ll run for the pilot. High level tasks and owners: 

Day -7 to Day 0 (prep)
- Marissa: Create pilot dashboard + metric contract (p50/p95/p99 latency, token rate, errors, cache-hit) and share read-only link (ETA 2028-08-06).
- Ben: Confirm reserved capacity sizing and budget approval.
- Anna/Lumenix: Provide 48-hour traffic export, golden prompts, IP allowlist, and request-id header sample (ETA 2028-08-02).

Pilot execution (2028-08-09 to 2028-08-12)
- Run smoke test first 2 hours (baseline), then progressive spike tests up to full peak.
- Observe cache hit ratio and evaluate improvement opportunities (KV prefix caching).
- Execute fallback model test by simulating overload to ensure graceful degradation within decision criteria.

Post-pilot deliverables (within 3 business days)
- Full pilot report (Marissa) including L1/L2 metrics, a short interpretive summary, and recommended config changes (quantization, batch sizing, routing policy).
- Meeting to decide next steps (expand to dedicated commit or iterate on config).

Credentials / access needed from Lumenix
- Read-only S3 export location or short-lived upload for the traffic export.
- Allowlist for pilot runner: 52.21.0.0/20 (we will provide final CIDR).
- Optional: temporary service account for cross-correlation (recommend scoped API key).

I’ll provision the dashboard and share the links as soon as they’re ready. If anyone wants to push the pilot start a week earlier, we can try to accelerate but will need the traffic export ASAP.

—Marissa
